brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base with removable bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0). Removable bin trays: hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) in cell 0,0,0 and hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) in cell 1,0,0. Bins drop into their cells and are not bolted.
Drawer notch frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) at notch 0,1,0 between the two bases.
Cover (full, top) on cell 0,0,0 with a handle (chain) on its top face. Only the configurator's fit and collision checks were run; I did not verify the handle's load capacity.
Compact two-cell build with a handle; actual weight depends on the print material and infill, which the configurator does not model. Print estimate is about 1651 g of filament-equivalent budget.

finish.summary: Built a two-base electronics organizer: two full hex bases with a 3-compartment bin and a 2-compartment bin, a drawer frame notch between them, a top cover with a carry handle on the first base, and house rules applied (open faces capped, joints locked). check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. Props were not added since the brief is about the parts. Material strength and weight were not assessed.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
